messages:
From: Rachael Owens <rachael@lumenbank.com>

Cc: LumenBank SRE <sre@lumenbank.com>
Date: 2027-12-01 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency + 5xx spike — urgent

Tessa —

We started seeing a sustained latency increase (p95 up from ~120ms to ~950ms) and a wave of 5xx errors beginning ~08:40 PT. This is happening on our reserved pool (UUID: LB-RES-09) and is impacting user-facing debit authorization flows. Our SRE has captured traces and token counts; attaching a short sample.

We expected reserved capacity to provide consistent throughput; instead the pool appears constrained and requests are being rate-limited/failing. Can you confirm whether this is a customer-side misrouting, a model variant fallback, or a backend saturation? We need a bridge and an ETA — this is affecting transactions.

Rachael
Head of Platform Engineering, LumenBank

Attachment: sample-traces.txt (5 KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spike — urgent

Rachael — thank you for the heads up and the traces. We’re escalating immediately.

Immediate actions I’ve kicked off:
- Ops: Jonas is spinning up an emergency bridge (jad: joining).
- Routing: We’re checking reserved pool saturation and whether requests are spilling to a lower-capacity variant.
- Short-term mitigation: request routing to a hosted fallback is being prepared if we confirm slot exhaustion.

Can you grant us a short sample of request IDs (the top 10 by error rate) and confirm if you’ve recently increased burst traffic (e.g., new batch jobs)? That will help triage whether this is demand spike vs internal scheduling (rebalancer, maintenance).

I’ll update in the bridge — joining in 5.

— Tessa

Subject: Fwd: Prod latency + 5xx spike — reserved capacity check (ops readout)

Folks — quick ops readout from the bridge (notes):
- Observed behavior: LB-RES-09 shows sustained queue depth increase on the NVLink fabric for the pool. Token consumption is within expected range but scheduling latency for KV-cache warmups is spiking (cold-cache misses across many shards).
- Impact: Requests are timing out behind the quota guard; we’re seeing 429s escalate to 5xx in downstream inference workers.
- Candidate causes: simultaneous KV cache invalidation coupled with a maintenance window that moved several workers to a single rack (reducing effective parallelism).

Immediate asks for exec/ops:
1) Authorize a temporary 30% burst from shared capacity to LB-RES-09 for up to 3 hours (manual entitlement).
2) Permit a rapid, targeted rollback of last-night kernel change on the pool (reverts only model-serving kernel selector to previous stable).
3) Approve fallback routing to a quantized compatible variant (model: open-q2-small) for latency-sensitive endpoints while we heal caches.

I recommend leadership sign-off on (1) and (3) immediately; (2) requires an ops change window but is low-risk.

Attachments: incident-timeline.pdf (timeline + metrics), lumenbank-token-usage.csv

— Jonas
Director, Site Reliability

Date: 2027-12-01 13:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Prod latency + 5xx spike — reserved capacity short-term mitigations

Rachael — thank you for your patience. Quick summary and next steps: 

What happened (summary):
- Root cause: unexpected KV-cache invalidation across LB-RES-09 during a narrow maintenance window reduced effective parallelism on the rack and amplified cold-cache penalties. The resulting queueing pushed requests beyond the reserved throughput envelope, hitting quota guards and producing 5xx responses.

What we did (immediate mitigations):
- Authorized manual 30% burst from shared capacity to LB-RES-09 (effective at 12:10 PT) — that reduced queue depth by ~60% within 20 minutes.
- Activated fallback routing for latency-critical endpoints to the quantized model (open-q2-small) — p95 fell from ~950ms to ~180ms for the affected route.
- Rolled back the kernel selector change on the affected pool at 12:35 PT (low-risk revert) — improved cache warmup behavior across workers.

Customer-facing ask and credits: 
- We’d like to offer LumenBank a one-time service credit covering estimated token overage and a goodwill credit for the incident. Marissa, can you own the credit approval (estimate in attached CSV)?

Follow-ups (post-mortem actions):
- Ops will add a KV-cache pre-warm during maintenance windows and block single-rack consolidations for reserved pools (Jonas to lead).
- Product will add an SLO-checker that flags pool fragmentation risk before scheduler moves (Vivek to prioritize).
- We will schedule a 30-min post-mortem with LumenBank on Monday to walk the timeline & proposed guardrails.

Bridge recording and docs: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20271201-47

Thanks again — we’ll hold the PM + SRE follow-up and make sure the credits are ready before EOW.

— Tessa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: incident-timeline.pdf, lumenbank-token-usage.csv
